concepts.title: Classification of Materials - Solids, Liquids, Gases
concepts.definition: Materials are classified as solids, liquids, or gases based on their shape, volume, and how tightly their particles are packed.
concepts.key_idea: Solids have a fixed shape and volume, liquids have a fixed volume but take the shape of the container, and gases have neither a fixed shape nor a fixed volume.
question_patterns: how are materials classified into solids liquids and gases
what is the difference between a solid and a liquid
which state of matter has a fixed shape and fixed volume
why do gases have no fixed shape or volume
give two examples each of solids liquids and gases

solution_steps.action: Observe the shape of the material
solution_steps.explain: Check whether the material keeps its own shape (solid), takes the shape of the container (liquid), or fills the whole container (gas).

solution_steps.action: Observe the volume of the material
solution_steps.explain: Check whether the material has a fixed volume (solid and liquid) or expands to fill any container (gas).

solution_steps.action: Classify the material as solid, liquid, or gas
solution_steps.explain: Fixed shape and volume -> solid; fixed volume but changing shape -> liquid; no fixed shape or volume -> gas.

worked_examples.question: Classify a stone, water, and air as solid, liquid, or gas.
worked_examples.solution: A stone has a fixed shape and volume, so it is a solid. Water has a fixed volume but takes the shape of its container, so it is a liquid. Air has no fixed shape or volume and fills any container, so it is a gas.
worked_examples.answer: Stone - solid; Water - liquid; Air - gas.

worked_examples.question: Why does a gas have neither a fixed shape nor a fixed volume?
worked_examples.solution: The particles of a gas are far apart and move freely, so a gas spreads to fill the shape and volume of any container it is placed in.
worked_examples.answer: Because gas particles are far apart and move freely, filling any container.

exercises.question: State two differences between solids and liquids.
Give one example each of a solid, a liquid, and a gas found at home.

concepts.title: Properties of Materials - Hardness
concepts.definition: Hardness is the property of a material that describes how difficult it is to scratch, dent, or compress it.
concepts.key_idea: Hard materials like iron and diamond resist scratching, while soft materials like sponge and chalk are easily scratched or compressed.
question_patterns: what is hardness of a material
which material is harder iron or sponge
how do we compare the hardness of two materials
give two examples of hard and soft materials
why is a diamond called a hard material

solution_steps.action: Select two materials to compare
solution_steps.explain: Choose the materials whose hardness you wish to compare, such as iron and sponge.

solution_steps.action: Test resistance to scratching or compression
solution_steps.explain: Try to scratch or press each material; the one that resists scratching and compression is harder, and the one that is easily marked is softer.

solution_steps.action: Classify as hard or soft
solution_steps.explain: Rank the materials by hardness: hard materials resist scratching (e.g., iron, diamond), while soft materials are easily scratched or compressed (e.g., sponge, chalk).

worked_examples.question: Which is harder -- iron or sponge -- and why?
worked_examples.solution: Iron resists scratching and compression, so it is hard. Sponge is easily compressed, so it is soft. Therefore iron is harder than sponge.

worked_examples.question: Why is diamond called the hardest natural material?
worked_examples.solution: Diamond cannot be scratched by any other natural material, which is why it is called the hardest natural material.
worked_examples.answer: Diamond resists scratching by all other natural materials.

exercises.question: Define hardness and give one example each of a hard and a soft material.
Explain how you would test which of two materials is harder.

concepts.title: Properties of Materials - Transparency
concepts.definition: Transparency is the property of a material that describes how much light can pass through it; materials are classified as transparent, translucent, or opaque.
concepts.key_idea: Transparent materials allow light to pass through clearly, translucent materials allow partial passage of light, and opaque materials do not allow any light to pass through.
question_patterns: what is transparency of a material
what is the difference between transparent and opaque
give examples of transparent translucent and opaque materials
is a glass window transparent or opaque
classify paper glass and wood by transparency

solution_steps.action: Place the material between a light source and the eye
solution_steps.explain: Hold the material in front of a light source and observe how much light passes through it.

solution_steps.action: Observe how clearly objects can be seen through it
solution_steps.explain: If objects are seen clearly, the material is transparent; if seen dimly, it is translucent; if nothing is seen, it is opaque.

solution_steps.action: Classify as transparent, translucent, or opaque
solution_steps.explain: Glass is transparent, butter paper is translucent, and wood or metal is opaque, based on how much light passes through.

worked_examples.question: Classify glass, butter paper, and wood as transparent, translucent, or opaque.
worked_examples.solution: Glass allows light to pass through clearly, so it is transparent. Butter paper allows partial light, so it is translucent. Wood does not allow any light, so it is opaque.
worked_examples.answer: Glass - transparent; Butter paper - translucent; Wood - opaque.

worked_examples.question: Why can we see through a glass window but not through a wooden door?
worked_examples.solution: Glass is transparent and allows light to pass through so objects behind it are visible. Wood is opaque and blocks light completely, so nothing can be seen through it.
worked_examples.answer: Glass is transparent; wood is opaque.

exercises.question: Define transparent, translucent, and opaque materials with one example each.
Classify the following as transparent, translucent, or opaque: clear plastic, oiled paper, cardboard.

concepts.title: Properties of Materials - Solubility
concepts.definition: Solubility is the property that describes whether a material dissolves in a liquid (solvent) to form a uniform mixture called a solution.
concepts.key_idea: Soluble substances like salt and sugar dissolve in water, while insoluble substances like sand and chalk powder do not; some liquids like oil are immiscible with water.
question_patterns: what is solubility
which substances are soluble in water
is salt soluble or insoluble in water
why does oil not dissolve in water
give two examples of soluble and insoluble substances

solution_steps.action: Add the material to a solvent such as water
solution_steps.explain: Place the material in a container of water and stir it to check whether it dissolves.

solution_steps.action: Observe whether the material dissolves
solution_steps.explain: If the material disappears and forms a uniform mixture, it is soluble; if it remains visible or settles, it is insoluble.

solution_steps.action: Classify as soluble or insoluble
solution_steps.explain: Salt and sugar are soluble in water, while sand, chalk powder, and oil are insoluble, based on whether they dissolve.

worked_examples.question: Is salt soluble or insoluble in water?
worked_examples.solution: When salt is added to water and stirred, it dissolves completely to form a uniform salt solution, so salt is soluble in water.

worked_examples.question: Why does oil form a separate layer when mixed with water?
worked_examples.solution: Oil is insoluble in water and does not mix with it, so it forms a separate layer on top of the water.
worked_examples.answer: Oil is insoluble in water and forms a separate layer.

exercises.question: Define solubility and give two examples each of soluble and insoluble substances in water.
Explain why sand is called insoluble in water.

concepts.title: Metals and Non-Metals
concepts.definition: Metals are materials that are typically hard, lustrous, malleable, ductile, and good conductors of heat and electricity; non-metals lack these properties.
concepts.key_idea: Metals like iron, copper, and aluminium are shiny and conduct heat and electricity, while non-metals like sulphur, carbon, and oxygen are dull and are poor conductors.
question_patterns: what are metals and non-metals
give two properties of metals
is iron a metal or non-metal
what is lustre in metals
how are metals different from non-metals

solution_steps.action: Observe the appearance of the material
solution_steps.explain: Check whether the material is shiny (lustrous), which is a property of metals, or dull, which is typical of non-metals.

solution_steps.action: Test for hardness, malleability, and conduction
solution_steps.explain: Metals are generally hard, can be beaten into sheets (malleable), drawn into wires (ductile), and conduct heat and electricity; non-metals are usually soft and poor conductors.

solution_steps.action: Classify as metal or non-metal
solution_steps.explain: If the material is lustrous, hard, malleable, ductile, and a good conductor, it is a metal (e.g., iron, copper); otherwise it is a non-metal (e.g., sulphur, carbon).

worked_examples.question: List three properties that distinguish metals from non-metals.
worked_examples.solution: Metals are lustrous (shiny), malleable and ductile, and good conductors of heat and electricity. Non-metals are usually dull, brittle, and poor conductors.
worked_examples.answer: Metals are lustrous, malleable/ductile, and good conductors; non-metals are dull, brittle, and poor conductors.

worked_examples.question: Is copper a metal or a non-metal? Give a reason.
worked_examples.solution: Copper is shiny, can be drawn into wires, and conducts electricity well, so it is a metal.
worked_examples.answer: Copper is a metal because it is lustrous, ductile, and a good conductor.

exercises.question: State any three properties of metals with examples.
Classify the following as metal or non-metal: aluminium, sulphur, gold, carbon.

concepts.title: Natural and Synthetic Materials
concepts.definition: Natural materials are obtained directly from nature (plants, animals, or the earth), while synthetic materials are made by humans through chemical processes.
concepts.key_idea: Wood, cotton, and leather are natural, whereas plastics, nylon, and synthetic fibres are man-made (synthetic).
question_patterns: what are natural and synthetic materials
is cotton natural or synthetic
give two examples of synthetic materials
how is plastic different from wood
why are synthetic materials called man-made

solution_steps.action: Identify the source of the material
solution_steps.explain: Determine whether the material comes directly from nature (plants, animals, earth) or is produced in a factory through chemical processes.

solution_steps.action: Check whether the material has been chemically manufactured
solution_steps.explain: If the material is created by humans using chemicals, it is synthetic; if it is obtained in a ready form from nature, it is natural.

solution_steps.action: Classify as natural or synthetic
solution_steps.explain: Wood, cotton, and leather are natural materials, while plastic, nylon, and polyester are synthetic materials.

worked_examples.question: Classify cotton and nylon as natural or synthetic.
worked_examples.solution: Cotton is obtained from plants, so it is natural. Nylon is made by humans through chemical processes, so it is synthetic.

worked_examples.question: Why is plastic called a synthetic material?
worked_examples.solution: Plastic is produced in factories by chemical processing of petroleum and does not occur naturally, so it is called a synthetic (man-made) material.
worked_examples.answer: Plastic is man-made, produced by chemical processes, so it is synthetic.

exercises.question: Define natural and synthetic materials with one example each.
Classify the following as natural or synthetic: wood, polyester, leather, plastic.

concepts.title: Uses of Materials Based on Properties
concepts.definition: Materials are chosen for specific uses based on their properties such as hardness, transparency, conductivity, solubility, and lustre.
concepts.key_idea: The property of a material decides its use -- metals are used for wires because they conduct electricity, glass for windows because it is transparent, and plastics for handles because they are insulators.
question_patterns: why are metals used to make electric wires
why is glass used to make windows
why are cooking utensils made of metals
how does the property of a material decide its use
why are plastic handles used on cooking pans

solution_steps.action: Identify the required property for the use
solution_steps.explain: Determine what property the object needs, such as conductivity for wires or transparency for windows.

solution_steps.action: Match the property to a suitable material
solution_steps.explain: Select a material that has the required property, e.g., metals for conduction, glass for transparency, plastic for insulation.

solution_steps.action: Justify the choice of material
solution_steps.explain: Explain that the material is chosen because its property matches the need, such as copper for wires because it conducts electricity well.

worked_examples.question: Why are electric wires made of copper?
worked_examples.solution: Copper is a metal and a good conductor of electricity, so it allows electric current to flow easily, which is why it is used for wires.
worked_examples.answer: Copper is used because it is a good conductor of electricity.

worked_examples.question: Why is glass used to make windows?
worked_examples.solution: Glass is transparent, allowing light to pass through, so it is used for windows to let in light while keeping out wind and rain.
worked_examples.answer: Glass is transparent, so it lets light pass through.

exercises.question: Explain with two examples how the property of a material decides its use.
Why are the handles of cooking pans made of plastic and not metal?

concepts.title: Mixtures and Pure Substances
concepts.definition: A pure substance is made of only one kind of material, while a mixture contains two or more substances that are not chemically combined and can be separated by physical methods.
concepts.key_idea: Pure substances like distilled water and sugar have fixed composition, while mixtures like salt water and air contain more than one substance mixed together.
question_patterns: what is the difference between a mixture and a pure substance
is salt water a mixture or pure substance
give two examples of mixtures
what is a pure substance
can the components of a mixture be separated

solution_steps.action: Examine the composition of the material
solution_steps.explain: Check whether the material is made of only one kind of substance or contains more than one substance.

solution_steps.action: Determine whether the components are chemically combined
solution_steps.explain: In a pure substance the components are not separable by physical means, while in a mixture the components are only physically mixed and can be separated.

solution_steps.action: Classify as pure substance or mixture
solution_steps.explain: If the material has a fixed composition of one substance, it is pure (e.g., distilled water, sugar); if it contains two or more physically mixed substances, it is a mixture (e.g., salt water, air).

worked_examples.question: Is salt water a pure substance or a mixture? Explain.
worked_examples.solution: Salt water contains two substances -- salt and water -- that are physically mixed and can be separated by evaporation, so it is a mixture.
worked_examples.answer: Salt water is a mixture because it contains salt and water that can be separated physically.

worked_examples.question: Give one example each of a pure substance and a mixture.
worked_examples.solution: Distilled water is a pure substance because it contains only water. Air is a mixture because it contains several gases such as nitrogen, oxygen, and carbon dioxide.
worked_examples.answer: Pure substance - distilled water; Mixture - air.

exercises.question: Distinguish between a pure substance and a mixture with one example each.
Classify the following as pure substance or mixture: sugar, lemonade, distilled water, soil.
